A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EgoM2P and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Existing content can be matched reliably; v3 adds Appendix E.

before.justification: v1 reports original camera-tracking, gaze-estimation, depth-estimation, and video-synthesis experiments, plus appendix ablations and quantization-error analysis.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds a qualitative 4D reconstruction comparison and reconstruction timings against MegaSaM.

M1.justification: The tokenizers, architecture, losses, masking, sampling, and inference algorithms are unchanged. Appendix E demonstrates another application without documenting a new method component or procedural adaptation.

E1.justification: Appendix E adds an egocentric dynamic 4D reconstruction demonstration using video and ground-truth camera intrinsics. Existing training and evaluation datasets are retained; no additional named dataset is identified.

E2.justification: MegaSaM is newly evaluated against EgoM2P for reconstruction in Appendix E and Figure E.1. Comparator membership in all existing experiments remains unchanged.

E3.justification: The added reconstruction evaluation supplies ground-truth intrinsics and compares runtime using a two-second, 8 FPS video. These are conditions for the new experiment; existing splits, metrics, training budgets, and evaluation procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure E.1 adds a qualitative case study comparing dynamic scene reconstructions from EgoM2P and MegaSaM, extending the earlier separate depth and trajectory visualizations. Existing token-count, sampling-weight, EgoGen, and quantization analyses are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed-based variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new reconstruction timings are point estimates without added uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Appendix E newly reports reconstruction taking less than 1 second for EgoM2P versus 71 seconds for MegaSaM on a two-second, 8 FPS video, alongside qualitative outputs. Existing benchmark and appendix result values are unchanged; this is an added comparison, not improved performance between versions.

T1.justification: Modality definitions, tokenizer and prediction losses, Dirichlet sampling formulas, and inference mathematics are unchanged. No new theoretical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same multimodal multitasking, 4D understanding, performance, and efficiency claims. Appendix E supplies additional evidence without redefining those core claims.

C2.justification: Existing generalization interpretations, quantization discussion, and tokenizer limitations are retained. Appendix E reiterates the established efficiency contrast with optimization-heavy specialists rather than introducing a new mechanism explanation or limitation.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, training times, and code-access statements are unchanged. The sampling cross-reference and masking typo correction clarify information already present in v1; Appendix E provides no additional reconstruction implementation or timing-hardware details.

R1.justification: v3 adds the MegaSaM reference and a narrow comparison with its depth-estimation and geometry-optimization approach. Existing references and broader positioning relative to foundation models and 4M are retained despite citation renumbering.

P1.justification: v3 appends a short reconstruction section, refines sampling wording and adds an Appendix A.2 cross-reference in Section 3.3, and corrects 'make out' to 'mask out' in Appendix A.1. The remaining narrative and section organization are stable.

P2.justification: Figure E.1 adds two reconstruction visualizations with method and runtime labels on the final appendix page. Existing figures and table structures remain unchanged, with limited text and bibliography reflow.

improvement.justification: Appendix E and Figure E.1 modestly strengthen the existing 4D applicability and efficiency claims through a direct reconstruction example and MegaSaM timing comparison. Missing quantitative reconstruction accuracy and timing-hardware details limit the strength of this addition. Existing evidence is preserved, and small editorial corrections improve clarity.
